title: Circumstances and Character
gist_ar: مقال بيناقش هل الظروف ولا الشخصية اللي تحدّد النتايج.
text:
If I were a more patient person, I would have handled that meeting better. Perhaps. But if my circumstances had been different, I might be a more patient person now — and that is the harder thought.

We like explanations based on character. He is disorganised; she is confident. Such descriptions feel permanent, which is convenient, because permanent things require no action. Yet if you had been born into a different position, with different priorities and responsibilities, you would probably describe your own character differently today.

This does not remove responsibility. A person who is qualified and wealthy still chooses how to behave. The point is narrower: when we explain an outcome entirely by character, we usually stop looking, and the circumstances that influenced it survive untouched to affect the next person.

A practical test is to ask what would have to change for this behaviour to become unnecessary. If the honest answer is 'nothing — he is simply like that', character may be the explanation. If the answer names a deadline, a workload or a lack of training, then we were never describing a character at all.
